$comment: The pins for every sandbox image Ship builds. ONE source of truth:
images/build.sh reads this file and passes the values as build args, and
src/harness.ts:HARNESS_PACKAGES mirrors `harnesses` with a test that fails
if the two drift (src/harness.test.ts).
Why any of this is pinned at all: before 2026-08-26 the images were built
by hand from Dockerfiles that lived only in ~ on deploy-test, from moving
tags. Nothing outside that box could reproduce them, and nothing recorded
what a given run's sandbox actually contained.
Bumping a harness version is a DELIBERATE act: selectAdapter (src/harness.ts)
refuses to replay a run under a program other than the one that wrote its
log, and the vendor binary is that program. Bump, rebuild, redeploy — never
let the image drift under a running worker.
Debian 13 (trixie) for both, which is what the production sandbox image
has actually been running (python 3.13, git 2.47). Digests are the
multi-arch index digests: a tag moves, a digest does not.
GO 1.25, NOT 1.24. Bumped 2026-08-26 because three repos need 1.25 and
on a 1.24 sandbox every Go pull request arrived marked `tests: failed` —
a base-image mismatch read as the agent's fault, which cost a day (see
the same date in src/tests.ts:preExisting). Do NOT pin this back to 1.24.

$comment_rust: rust is a moving 1.x tag, not a digest, on purpose: Nucleus tracks stable
Rust and a digest would need bumping every six weeks to keep its MSRV.

$comment: The vendor coding agents an external harness adapter drives
(src/harness-external.ts). `id` matches HARNESS_VERSIONS in
src/harness.ts and the `harness` field of a project record.
claude-code is the one verified on deploy-test 2026-08-24. opencode
moved to v2 (D6): the 1.x opencode-ai line ends at 1.19.3, the 2.x
CLI is @opencode/cli, and the pin is the exact 2.0.26 build the
measured v2 event contract was taken from
(evals/receipts/2026-10-14-opencode-v2-events.txt; 2.0.32 was the
line's latest when this pin was set). The adapter drives both the 1.x
and 2.x contracts and refuses anything past 2.x, so an image that
still bakes 1.18.23 keeps working until it is rebuilt.

$comment_acp: The ACP harness pins (E7 H3) are the exact versions the H0 receipts
protocolVersion 1. cursor is NOT here on purpose: it is a registry
binary, not npm, and its pin lands with H9's build-time registry support.
images/acp-driver/ship-acp.mjs (the in-sandbox ACP driver) is baked into
every image regardless of which harnesses are declared.
